I will keep most of my land in the wheat-maize rotation and only leave a smaller piece for cotton. On 8 mu, I will use 6 mu for winter wheat followed by summer maize, and 2 mu for cotton. That is the balance I would choose because wheat-maize fits my land and water conditions best, gives me grain from two seasons, and is easier to manage across the year when some family labor is away working off-farm. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on that to protect wheat at key growth stages and to support maize after sowing if rainfall is short. For wheat, I will use improved seed, moderate-high nitrogen, enough phosphorus, some potassium, rotary tillage, and a small number of pesticide sprays because I want stable grain yield without making the field too costly to manage. For maize, I will use hybrid seed because I want strong yield on the same wheat land after harvest, with slightly higher nitrogen and fewer irrigations than wheat. For cotton, I will keep only 2 mu because it needs more labor and more plant protection work, but I will still grow it as a cash crop; I will use improved seed, keep potassium higher than grain crops, irrigate a few times, and spray more often because insects are a bigger risk there. My goal is steady output, manageable labor, and lower risk across the whole year.
